pages.en:
The hands of the clock turn.

It is a little after nine in the morning.

Two hours have passed since, at Tohsaka's instruction, I carried Sakura in from where she lay collapsed near the gate.

My head, numb with sleep, is finally beginning to work properly again.

The clock ticks.
It’s past nine o’clock.
It’s been two hours since I carried Sakura in from where she’d collapsed by the entrance.
Function is finally returning to my numbed mind.

What in the world is wrong with me?

There are mountains of things I need to think about.

Sakura's condition after collapsing with a fever.

The enemy's massive feeding last night.

I’d be embarrassed if somebody changed my clothes while I was sleeping, so Tohsaka’s completely right.

pages.ja: 「ま、今は我慢するんだな。病人は病人らしく休まないと損だぞ？ なにしろ、治ったら朝も昼も夜も桜に押し付けるつもりなんだ。後になって、あの時もっと休んどけば良かったって後悔するぞ」
pages.jaRuby: 「ま、今は我慢するんだな。病人は病人らしく休まないと損だぞ？ なにしろ、治ったら朝も昼も夜も桜に押し付けるつもりなんだ。後になって、あの時もっと休んどけば良かったって後悔するぞ」
pages.en: “You'll have to be patient for now. If you don't rest properly when you're sick, you're only cheating yourself. Once you're better, I plan to leave breakfast, lunch, and dinner to you every day. You'll regret not enjoying the chance to rest while you had it.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Well, just bear it for now. A sick person has to rest like one. After all, I’m going to leave you in charge of breakfast, lunch, and dinner once you get well. You’ll regret not resting more then.”

pages.ja:
冗談っぽく、本気で今後の方針を口にする。
……ああ。
桜がそれで嬉しいのなら、むこう半年ぐらい厨房を預けよう。
pages.jaRuby:

……ああ。
桜がそれで嬉しいのなら、むこう半年ぐらい厨房を預けよう。
pages.en:
I say it like a joke, though I mean every word as a plan for our future.

…Yes.

If that will make Sakura happy, I will surrender the kitchen to her for the next six months.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I jokingly say what I plan to do.
…Yeah.
I can leave her in charge of cooking for about half a year if that’ll please her.

pages.ja:
「
ホントですか？ 先輩、あとでやっぱりなしっていうのはダメですよ？」
「本当だって。とりあえず半年は大人しくしてる。
あー、いや、桜がタイヘンな時は助手として、コンロ番ぐらいはさせてもらいたいけど」
こっちも八年近く台所に立っていたのだ。
やはり少しは鍋を持たないと落ち着かない。

pages.en:
“—Really? You're not allowed to take it back later, Shirou.”

“Really. I'll stay out of the way for at least six months.

“Well—when you have too much to handle, I'd like you to let me assist. I could at least mind the stove.”

I have spent nearly eight years in the kitchen myself.

I doubt I could settle down without lifting a pot now and then.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Really? You can’t take it back later, okay?”
“I’m serious. I won’t do anything for at least half a year.
Well, I’d like to at least keep watch on the food on the gas burner when you need help.”
I’ve been standing in the kitchen for eight years.
I don’t feel at ease unless I’m holding a pan or something.

pages.ja:
「はい。じゃあ約束ですよ先輩？ わたしが治ったら、真っ先にごはんを食べてくださいね」
「ああ。そんな約束でよければ幾らでも」
pages.jaRuby:
「はい。じゃあ約束ですよ先輩？ わたしが治ったら、真っ先にごはんを食べてくださいね」
「ああ。そんな約束でよければ幾らでも」
pages.en:
“All right. Then it's a promise, Shirou. Once I'm better, you have to be the very first person to eat my cooking.”

“Of course. I'll make you as many promises like that as you want.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Okay, then it’s a promise. Please eat my meals once I get well.”
“Yeah. I’ll promise you all you want.”

pages.ja:
席を立つ。
これ以上話をして、桜を疲れさせる訳にはいかない。
話もできたし、桜の無事も確認できた。
今は一人で休ませてやるべきだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
席を立つ。
これ以上話をして、桜を疲れさせる訳にはいかない。
話もできたし、桜の無事も確認できた。
今は一人で休ませてやるべきだろう。
pages.en:
I rise from my chair.

I cannot exhaust Sakura by keeping her talking.

We have spoken, and I have reassured myself that she is all right.

For now, I should let her rest alone.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I get up.
I can’t keep talking to her and tire her.
We were able to talk, and I know Sakura’s doing fine.
I should let her rest now.

pages.ja:
「じゃあまた後で。昼メシ時になったら来るから、それまで眠ってるんだぞ」
ベッドから離れる。
桜は声を出さず、横になったままこくんと頷いた。
pages.jaRuby:
「じゃあまた後で。昼メシ時になったら来るから、それまで眠ってるんだぞ」
ベッドから離れる。
桜は声を出さず、横になったままこくんと頷いた。
pages.en:
“I'll see you later. I'll come back at lunchtime. Until then, get some sleep.”

I step away from the bed.

Sakura says nothing, merely giving a small nod where she lies.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Then I’ll see you later. I’ll come here again during lunch, so sleep until then.”
I step away from the bed.
Sakura nods silently.

pages.ja:
「
と。そうだ桜」
ドアノブに手をかけ、振り向かずに声をあげる。
pages.jaRuby:
「
と。そうだ桜」
ドアノブに手をかけ、振り向かずに声をあげる。
pages.en:
“—Oh, right. Sakura.”

My hand on the doorknob, I call to her without turning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh yeah, Sakura.”
I stop at the door and call out to her without turning around.

pages.ja:
「はい？ なんですか、先輩？」
「いや。なんで門の前でなんか倒れてたのかなって。
桜、俺の部屋で寝てただろ？」
できるだけ自然に問いかける。
桜はわずかに息を飲んだあと

pages.en:
“Yes? What is it, Shirou?”

“I was wondering why you collapsed in front of the gate.

“You fell asleep in my room, didn't you?”

I make the question as natural as I can.

Sakura draws the faintest breath, then—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes? What is it, Senpai?”
“Oh, I was wondering why you were collapsed in front of the house.
You were sleeping in my room, right?”
I try to ask as naturally as I can.
After a faint gasp…

pages.ja:
「朝の散歩です。先に目が覚めたから、少し外に出ようかなって。けどそこで倒れちゃいました。
ほんと、姉さんの言う通りですよね。今のわたしは、外に出たらダメみたいです」
そう、俺と同じぐらい、自然な明るさで返答した。
pages.jaRuby:
「朝の散歩です。先に目が覚めたから、少し外に出ようかなって。けどそこで倒れちゃいました。
ほんと、姉さんの言う通りですよね。今のわたしは、外に出たらダメみたいです」
そう、俺と同じぐらい、自然な明るさで返答した。
pages.en:
“I went for a walk. I woke up first and thought I might step outside for a little while, but then I collapsed.

“My sister was right, wasn't she? It seems I shouldn't leave the house in my condition.”

She answers with a brightness every bit as carefully natural as my own.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I was taking a morning walk. I woke up early, so I went outside, but then I collapsed.
Nee-san’s right. I shouldn’t be going outside right now.”
…She replies as naturally as I asked her.
